tierWindow.goal: Articulate and critique creativity as a graduate attribute, that is innovation, enterprise and professional judgement, and integrate it into your own development as an advanced learner.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Analysis, evaluation, synthesis and self-direction (appraise, critique, integrate, justify).

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner is an experienced student, late in their degree or beyond, who already treats creativity as a usable academic skill and has applied creative methods in their work. This course assumes that grounding and turns to creativity as a professional and developmental attribute: innovation, enterprise, self-regulation and scholarly judgement.

decidedValue.courseOutcomeCountReason: Three, matching the three advanced strands: creativity as a professional attribute (innovation and enterprise), creativity turned on your own development (self-regulation), and creativity at work in scholarship (interpretation and debate). The advanced tier does not re-teach what creativity is or how to apply creative methods to set tasks; those belong to the introductory and intermediate tiers. It articulates and critiques creativity as an attribute the experienced learner already uses.

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three lessons. First, creativity as a graduate attribute: why innovation and enterprise are prized, and how creativity relates to adaptability. Second, creative self-regulation: how you monitor and amend your own strategies as a self-directed learner. Third, creativity in scholarly discourse: how imagination and interpretation open up debate around a source. Work through them in order.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This is an advanced course on creativity: not what creativity is, but what it is worth. By the end you will be able to appraise creativity as a graduate attribute that drives innovation and enterprise, integrate creative self-regulation into your own development, and critique how creativity operates in scholarly interpretation and debate.

You already treat creativity as a usable academic skill. The question now is more demanding. Why do disciplines, employers and research communities prize creativity so highly, and how do you exercise it deliberately in your own work and judgement?
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: appraise creativity as a graduate attribute, integrate creative self-regulation, critique creativity in scholarly discourse.

practiceConnection.academic: Creativity is named explicitly among the graduate attributes that disciplines and employers look for, alongside adaptability and flexibility. It is also the engine of original scholarship, where new readings and syntheses move a field forward. Treat this course as being about the creativity your own degree and future work will reward, not creativity in the abstract.

decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Creativity is no longer only a study skill: it is an attribute you can argue for and exercise deliberately. You can appraise creativity as a graduate attribute that drives innovation and enterprise, and say why it transfers beyond any single task. You can integrate creative self-regulation into your own learning, amending a strategy when honest monitoring shows it has stalled. And you can critique how creativity works in scholarship, opening up the discourse around a source and justifying a reading of your own.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, creativity is something you exercise in every advanced task. Each problem with no routine solution, each strategy you amend rather than repeat, each interpretation you open up and argue, is the attribute at work. It is also what research and professional life reward: the capacity to generate and defend new options under uncertainty travels well beyond your degree.
